hero.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes during Florida test
hero.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a static fire test at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station's Launch Complex 36 in Florida on Thursday evening. The explosion occurred at 9pm ET seconds after the scheduled "hotfire" test began, creating a massive fireball that destroyed the launchpad. The blast was visible across Florida's space coast, with an orange glow seen as far south as Fort Pierce, 185 kilometers away.

The incident threatens NASA's ambitious timeline for lunar exploration. NASA had just announced on Tuesday that Blue Origin won a contract to launch the first of three planned missions this year to begin construction of a $20 billion moon base. The New Glenn rocket is also the vehicle Blue Origin intends to use to deliver landers to the moon for NASA's Artemis program, including crewed landers for future astronaut missions.

Jeff Bezos, Blue Origin's founder, confirmed that all company employees were safe and uninjured. He described it as "a very rough day" on social media, stating that the company was already investigating the cause. "It's too early to know the root cause but we're already working to find it," Bezos said. "Very rough day, but we'll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying. It's worth it."

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman acknowledged the difficulty of developing heavy-lift rockets. "Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult," he posted. NASA said it would conduct a full evaluation of timeline impacts following a thorough investigation of the anomaly.

The explosion represents another significant setback for Blue Origin as it competes with SpaceX for NASA contracts. Last month, a payload from the third New Glenn flight ended up in the wrong orbit, prompting the Federal Aviation Administration to ground the rocket temporarily. Thursday's test was the first static fire test since the FAA cleared the vehicle to return to flight the previous week.

The incident has implications for NASA's lunar goals. The Artemis III mission, planned for 2027, will test Blue Origin's Blue Moon lander. Artemis IV, scheduled for 2028, will mark the first time humans return to the moon since 1972, with either Blue Origin or SpaceX providing the lunar lander.

Shockwaves from the explosion were felt across Florida's Atlantic coast, with residents reporting shaking homes in Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach. Emergency officials reported no threat from fumes or other hazards, though flames continued burning at the launchpad more than two hours after the blast. Residents and aerospace observers captured images and videos of the fiery plume that spread across the night sky.

cards.headline: Americans Injured in Iranian Missile Strike on Kuwaiti Air Base
cards.body:
Americans were injured when Iran launched missiles at a Kuwaiti air base, according to U.S. Central Command. The attack targeted facilities housing U.S. personnel.

The U.S. government characterized the strike as a violation of a fragile ceasefire between the two countries. Officials called the attack egregious, testing the terms of the truce.

The missile strike occurred as President Trump delayed making a final decision on an Iranian proposal. Trump had met with advisers at the White House for two hours to discuss a possible ceasefire extension, according to a senior administration official. Earlier, the president had suggested in a social media post that he was ready to make a decision.

U.S. and Iranian officials had previously confirmed they agreed on a framework for a deal. The framework under consideration would pause hostilities for two months. No deal was announced following the White House meeting.

The attack comes amid broader tensions in the region. Ships have been sailing with their transponders turned off to exit the Strait of Hormuz undetected, according to maritime data. About a quarter of large oil tankers that had been trapped by the conflict have escaped using this method.

Traffic through the strait has fallen as efforts to reopen the waterway have made little progress. A greater proportion of non-Iranian vessels are now crossing the strategic passage, according to recent data.

The Strait of Hormuz is a critical oil shipping route. Disruptions to traffic through the waterway affect global energy markets.

U.S. Central Command issued a statement on what it described as recent Iranian aggression. The command oversees U.S. military operations in the Middle East, including forces stationed in Kuwait and other Gulf states.

cards.headline: Pentagon says US ready to resume strikes on Iran without deal
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the United States is prepared to restart military operations against Iran if negotiations fail.
cards.body:
Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth stated the United States is fully capable of resuming military action against Iran. The comments came as President Trump met with advisers to make a final determination on a proposed framework agreement with Tehran that officials had confirmed both sides agreed to in principle.

Trump indicated he would remain patient while pursuing an agreement with Iran. However, no deal was announced following the White House meeting where Trump was expected to make his decision on whether to accept the tentative framework.

cards.headline: Trump meets advisers on Iran deal, makes no final decision
cards.teaser: The president met with his team to make a final determination on a framework deal with Iran but no announcement followed the meeting.
cards.body:
President Trump met with his advisers at the White House following confirmation that the US and Iran had agreed on a framework for a deal. However, no final decision was announced at the meeting.

The Pentagon has indicated the US is prepared to resume strikes on Iran if negotiations fail to produce an agreement.

cards.headline: Uganda Closes Border with Congo as Ebola Outbreak Grows
cards.teaser: Uganda shut its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo as suspected cases of a rare type of Ebola surge.
cards.body:
Uganda closed its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo following an outbreak of a rare Ebola strain known as the Bundibugyo virus. Ugandan health officials reported seven cases in the country, while suspected cases increased across the border in Congo.

The World Health Organization chief traveled to Congo's capital, Kinshasa, to support containment efforts. The WHO estimates the outbreak's death rate between 30% and 50% among confirmed cases. The organization has called for ceasefires among armed groups in the region to help prevent deaths from the preventable disease.

cards.headline: Hegseth Urges Asian Allies to Increase Defense Spending
cards.teaser: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told Asian allies the U.S. is not turning back on them but expects increased defense contributions.
cards.body:
Pete Hegseth addressed an Asian security summit in Singapore, emphasizing that the United States is not abandoning its regional allies while expecting them to increase defense spending. The U.S. defense secretary faced questions about American commitment to the region, including concerns about future arms deals.

Hegseth's remarks come as the U.S. seeks stronger burden-sharing among Asian partners in the face of regional security challenges.

cards.headline: Germany Deploys Troops to Lithuania Amid Russian Threat
cards.teaser: Berlin stationed forces in the Baltic country to protect against potential Russian aggression, welcomed by a nation once occupied by Germany.
cards.body:
Germany has deployed military forces to Lithuania to help protect the Baltic nation amid concerns over increased Russian aggression in Europe. This deployment represents a significant change in the relationship between the two countries, which have a complicated history.

Lithuania's welcome of German troops marks a notable shift. Despite being occupied by Germany during World War II, the country now views the German military presence as part of a new security arrangement designed to strengthen its defenses against contemporary threats.

cards.headline: Vietnam Leader Warns Asia About Superpower Conflict Risks
cards.teaser: Vietnamese leader To Lam cautioned that distrust and disregard for rules have created dangerous dynamics in the region.
cards.body:
To Lam spoke to military leaders from across Asia about the dangers of superpower competition. In his speech, the Vietnamese leader said distrust and a lack of respect for established rules had created a culture where the big fish swallow the small fish.

The warning came during a gathering of regional defense officials. Lam's comments addressed growing tensions as major powers increase their military presence and activities in Asia.

cards.teaser: Berlin stationed forces in the Baltic country to protect against potential Russian aggression, welcomed by a nation once occupied by Germany.

cards.headline: Japan's Immigration Rules Force Some Foreign Business Owners to Leave
cards.teaser: New visa policies under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi are affecting foreign entrepreneurs who have established roots in Japan.
cards.body:
Japanese immigration enforcement has caught curry shop owners and other foreign business operators in a broader crackdown. Under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, new visa rules are being applied more strictly.

The policy changes are forcing some foreign business owners who have put down roots in Japan to leave the country. The immigration measures represent a shift in how Japan handles foreign entrepreneurs and small business operators.

cards.headline: Spanish Prime Minister Faces Survival Fight Amid Corruption Probes
cards.teaser: Pedro Sánchez confronts mounting scandals as investigations into colleagues and relatives threaten his tenure.
cards.body:
Pedro Sánchez is fighting for political survival after eight years as Spain's prime minister. Corruption probes targeting his colleagues and relatives have created pressure on his leadership.

The wave of scandals has put Sánchez into what observers describe as a battle to remain in office. The investigations represent a significant challenge to his continued tenure as premier.

hero.headline: Death toll reaches nine in Washington paper mill explosion
hero.body:
Nine people are confirmed dead after a massive chemical tank explosion at a paper mill in Longview, Washington, with two workers still unaccounted for and presumed dead, according to reports from multiple news outlets.

The disaster occurred on Tuesday morning at the Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co facility when a tank containing more than 500,000 gallons of chemical mixture ruptured. The explosion released a caustic liquid capable of causing severe burns and lung injuries. Eight other people were injured in the blast, including a firefighter who responded to the emergency.

The chemical tank contained a caustic mixture used in the kraft pulping process to break down wood chips into paper pulp. White liquor, as the substance is called, can cause severe chemical burns on contact with skin and serious lung damage if inhaled.

Matt Amos, Longview fire battalion chief, explained that the six workers whose remains were initially recovered had been congregating in an area where employees gather during shift changes as they await their work assignments.

Among those confirmed dead was Gilbert Bernal, a grandfather who worked as an electrician at the plant. According to his friend Todd Cornwell, Bernal was known for his generosity. "He was one of the most genuinely good people that you've ever met. He would give you the shirt off his back if you needed it. He was always there willing to help in whatever needed to be done," Cornwell said.

CJ Doran, 26, was among those presumed dead. According to a verified fundraising post, he was a husband described as "the spiritual leader of their family, the joy of their home, and the family provider."

Other victims included John Forsberg, a father of two young children, and Jared Ammons, who had two children with another on the way. Braydon Finkas, an electrician at the plant, was also killed. His friend Rex Czuba described Finkas as deeply involved in his community. "He was a really big part of the town. He really jumped in and became a part of the community so quickly," Czuba said.

Recovery efforts have been slow and deliberate due to hazards posed by remaining chemicals and other industrial dangers. Crews have been avoiding the area closest to the tank out of concern for further collapse and have worked with engineers to determine whether damaged buildings around the tank are safe to enter. Workers must decontaminate remains before turning them over to the coroner's office for identification.

Authorities said the cause of the disaster remains under investigation and have not released the names of all victims. However, friends and relatives have begun confirming identities and posting online fundraisers to support the families of those killed.

The explosion represents one of the deadliest workplace accidents in the United States in recent decades.

cards.headline: Judge orders Trump's name removed from Kennedy Center
cards.teaser: A federal judge ruled that Trump's name must be removed from the Kennedy Center and blocked a planned closure of the facility.
cards.body:
A federal judge ordered the removal of Donald Trump's name from the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington, DC. US District Judge Christopher Cooper ruled that the prestigious performing arts venue cannot be renamed without an act of Congress. The judge directed the Trump administration to remove all physical signage bearing Trump's name and eliminate any references to a "Trump Kennedy Center" from official materials within 14 days.

Trump responded by saying he has "no interest" in the Kennedy Center following the court's decision.

cards.headline: Trump meets advisers on Iran deal, makes no final decision
cards.teaser: The president met with his team to make a final determination on a framework deal with Iran but no announcement followed the meeting.
cards.body:
President Trump met with his advisers at the White House following confirmation that the US and Iran had agreed on a framework for a deal. However, no final decision was announced at the meeting.

The Pentagon has indicated the US is prepared to resume strikes on Iran if negotiations fail to produce an agreement.

cards.headline: Bondi tells lawmakers redaction errors occurred in Epstein files release
cards.teaser: The former attorney general testified before a House panel about mistakes made when releasing files related to Jeffrey Epstein.
cards.body:
Pam Bondi defended her handling of the Epstein files during congressional testimony, acknowledging that redaction errors were made when the documents were released publicly. She attributed responsibility for the mistakes to Todd Blanche and Kash Patel.

The testimony occurred roughly a month after Bondi was dismissed as attorney general by President Donald Trump. By shifting blame to Blanche, Bondi has drawn Democratic scrutiny toward him as investigators examine the matter further.

cards.headline: Trump receives annual physical, doctor reports excellent health
cards.teaser: The White House released results from the president's latest medical examination showing he is fully fit to carry out his duties.
cards.body:
Trump's physician reported that the president is in excellent health and fully fit to carry out his duties, according to results released by the White House. The annual medical examination is part of routine monitoring for sitting presidents.

The doctor's assessment concluded that Trump is in overall excellent health. While the physician recommended increased exercise and weight loss, these suggestions did not change the overall favorable health evaluation.

cards.headline: Royal household received Prince Andrew emails six years ago
cards.teaser: Thousands of emails about the former prince's financial dealings were given to palace officials in 2020.
cards.body:
The Royal Household received thousands of emails about Prince Andrew's financial dealings in 2020, the BBC reports. The messages document the former prince's interactions with someone who served as his envoy.

The disclosure of these emails raises questions about what palace officials knew regarding Andrew's financial activities during that period.

cards.headline: SpaceX awarded $4.16 billion Space Force contract for satellite network
cards.teaser: The U.S. Space Force granted SpaceX a contract to build satellites that will track airborne targets.
cards.body:
SpaceX received a $4.16 billion contract from the U.S. Space Force to develop and deploy satellite systems for detecting and tracking airborne targets from orbit. The satellites will be equipped with sensors to identify threats globally, giving military commanders enhanced surveillance capabilities.

The contract is part of the Pentagon's "Golden Dome" defense system initiative. SpaceX has already secured substantial government contracts, generating one-fifth of its 2025 revenue from defense work ahead of its planned IPO.

cards.headline: Dell stock reaches all-time high on strong AI demand
cards.teaser: Dell shares soared after the company reported quarterly results driven by artificial intelligence server sales.
cards.body:
Dell stock jumped to a record high following the company's quarterly earnings report, which showed strong demand for AI servers. The surge added $34 billion to founder Michael Dell's personal wealth, placing him among the world's richest individuals.

The company's outlook reflected continued growth in its AI server business. Analysts described the quarter as a standout performance fueled by enterprise customers investing in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

cards.headline: Universal Music rejects Bill Ackman's $64 billion takeover offer
cards.teaser: The music company declined a buyout proposal from the billionaire investor's firm.
cards.body:
Universal Music Group turned down a $64 billion buyout proposal from Bill Ackman's Pershing Square, stating the offer significantly undervalued the business. Ackman, whose firm is a shareholder in the music company, had submitted a formal bid to take Universal private.

The rejection came despite Pershing Square's substantial stake in the company. Universal's decision to decline the proposal marks a setback for Ackman's acquisition efforts.

cards.headline: Oil prices decline as U.S. and Iran near cease-fire extension
cards.teaser: Energy markets reacted to signs that negotiators may reach an agreement to prolong a truce.
cards.body:
Oil prices fell as investors assessed tentative indications that the United States and Iran could extend a cease-fire. The diplomatic developments also drove fluctuations in stock markets.

Energy markets responded to the potential agreement, as crude oil prices are sensitive to Middle East tensions. Investors evaluated how a prolonged truce might reshape global oil supply and demand dynamics.

cards.headline: Southwest Airlines reverses extra-seat policy for plus-size passengers
cards.teaser: The carrier changed its seating rules after four months of public criticism.
cards.body:
Southwest Airlines modified its policy requiring some plus-size passengers to purchase additional seats. The airline updated the rule following sustained backlash from customers and advocacy groups.

The carrier implemented the original policy earlier this year but faced widespread criticism over its approach. Southwest has now adjusted how it handles seating accommodations for passengers who require extra space.

cards.headline: Penn Station train fire injures five, disrupts commuter service
cards.teaser: An Amtrak maintenance train caught fire near the New York transit hub during evening rush hour.
cards.body:
A fire broke out on an Amtrak maintenance train near Penn Station in New York during rush hour, injuring five people. The blaze disrupted service for both NJ Transit and Long Island Rail Road commuters who rely on the major transportation hub.

After firefighters extinguished the fire and cleared the area, Amtrak resumed service through Penn Station. The incident caused widespread delays and cancellations, affecting thousands of passengers traveling through the station.

hero.headline: Space Force awards SpaceX $6.45 billion in contracts ahead of IPO
hero.body:
The Space Force has awarded SpaceX $6.45 billion in new contracts as the company prepares for its initial public offering.

SpaceX revealed in its IPO filing that government contracts already accounted for one-fifth of its revenue in 2025. The new Space Force contracts add to that government revenue stream as the company transitions to public ownership.

The company filed for an IPO earlier this year, marking a shift from its long-standing private status. Founder Elon Musk had previously resisted taking the company public, citing concerns about quarterly reporting pressures and short-term thinking that could interfere with long-term goals like Mars colonization.

The $6.45 billion contract award represents a substantial portion of SpaceX's business. Based on the disclosed 20 percent government revenue figure from 2025, the company's total annual revenue would have been approximately $32.25 billion last year.

SpaceX has become a dominant player in the space launch industry through its reusable Falcon 9 rockets and Starship development program. The company also operates the Starlink satellite internet constellation, which provides global broadband coverage.

The Space Force, established as the newest branch of the U.S. military in 2019, relies heavily on commercial space companies for launch services. SpaceX competes with United Launch Alliance and other providers for these contracts.

Government contracts provide stable, predictable revenue streams that appeal to public market investors. The military and NASA have historically been major customers for commercial space launch providers.

The timing of the contract award just before the IPO could help SpaceX make a stronger case to potential investors. The backlog of government work provides visibility into future revenue.

SpaceX has not announced a target date for its public debut or disclosed other details about the planned IPO. The company will need to provide extensive financial disclosures to the Securities and Exchange Commission as part of the going-public process.

The contracts will fund Space Force missions over multiple years, though specific details about the launches and timelines were not disclosed in available reports.

cards.headline: Kenyan court blocks Trump administration plan to send Ebola-exposed Americans to Kenya
cards.teaser: A Kenyan court blocked a Trump administration plan to transport Americans exposed to Ebola to Kenya for quarantine.
cards.body:
A Kenyan court has blocked the Trump administration's plan to quarantine Americans exposed to Ebola in Kenya rather than returning them to the United States. The administration had been building a quarantine and treatment facility in Kenya for Americans affected by the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

The U.S. has existing specialized facilities designed specifically to handle Ebola-exposed individuals, making the Kenya arrangement redundant. Some health experts have criticized the approach, arguing that preventing Americans from returning home could undermine treatment efforts.

cards.headline: Proposed federal rules would allow grant cancellations without cause and make peer review optional
cards.teaser: The federal government has proposed new funding rules that would permit grant cancellations at any time and make peer review optional.
cards.body:
New proposed rules for federal research funding would permit the government to cancel grants at any time without specific cause. The changes would also make peer review optional for awarding grants.

Under the proposed system, political staff would screen grant applications for forbidden topics. The changes represent a shift from traditional scientific grant-making processes that have relied on expert peer review to evaluate research proposals on their scientific merit.

cards.headline: Indian court ruling on Google ad business draws support from startup founders
cards.teaser: An Indian court ruling related to Google's ad business has drawn support from startup founders and prompted legal analysis about trademarked keywords.
cards.body:
Startup founders are using an Indian court ruling to renew their criticism of Google's advertising practices. The decision specifically addresses how platforms manage trademarked keywords within their ad systems.

Legal experts believe the ruling could compel platforms to change their policies around trademarked keywords. The decision has resonated with company founders who have previously voiced concerns about Google's approach to advertising.

cards.headline: Researchers warn that AI-generated code may not produce better quality despite faster output
cards.teaser: Coders increasingly refuse to work without AI assistance, but researchers caution the technology may not improve code quality.
cards.body:
Software developers are increasingly refusing to work without AI assistance, relying on the technology to produce code faster. Researchers have issued warnings that this trend may create future problems.

While AI helps coders generate code more quickly, it may not be producing better quality code, according to researchers. The focus on speed over quality could cause problems down the road for developers who have become dependent on AI tools.

cards.headline: Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm tease Nvidia laptop processor announcement
cards.teaser: Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm have all posted teasers about upcoming Nvidia laptop processors ahead of an industry event.
cards.body:
Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm are jointly teasing the announcement of Nvidia's new N1X laptop processors ahead of Computex this weekend. Both the Windows and Nvidia GeForce accounts posted "A new era of PC" on X, with Arm following suit in the coordinated campaign.

Microsoft also teased new Surface hardware, with Windows and Surface chief Pavan Davuluri posting a mysterious image of what appears to be a curved display edge and referencing something new coming for developers.

cards.headline: Xbox confirms it will display PlayStation 5 availability information at upcoming showcase
cards.teaser: Xbox will show which games are available on PlayStation 5 during its upcoming Games Showcase event.
cards.body:
Xbox chief commercial officer Matt Booty confirmed that the company will display PlayStation 5 availability information for games during the upcoming Xbox Games Showcase. This marks a notable shift in how Xbox presents its gaming portfolio to audiences.

Games expected to be featured at the showcase include Gears of War E-Day and Fable. Booty also clarified that Project Helix will not be discussed during the event.

hero.headline: Golden Knights and Hurricanes to meet in Stanley Cup Final
hero.body:
The Vegas Golden Knights will face the Carolina Hurricanes in the Stanley Cup Final, the NHL announced. The series is scheduled to begin either June 2 or June 4.

The Hurricanes advanced to the final after defeating the Montreal Canadiens 6-1 in Game 5 of the Eastern Conference finals on Friday night. The victory marked Carolina's first Stanley Cup Final appearance in two decades. The team had lost three conference finals since 2019 before breaking through this season.

Carolina goaltender Frederik Andersen played in Friday's decisive game one day after his agent, Claude Lemieux, died by suicide. Andersen helped secure the win despite dealing with the personal tragedy.

The Golden Knights secured their spot in the championship round by advancing through the Western Conference playoffs. This will be their second appearance in the Stanley Cup Final since the franchise joined the NHL as an expansion team.

The Hurricanes will host Games 1 and 2 of the series at home in Raleigh. The NHL finalized the schedule with Game 1 set for June 2, though June 4 remains a possibility depending on scheduling factors.

Carolina last reached the Stanley Cup Final in 2006, when they won the championship. The franchise's only other final appearance came in 2002. The team's long drought made Friday's celebration particularly meaningful for players and fans who have waited years for another chance at the title.

Vegas is seeking its second Stanley Cup championship in franchise history. The team won the title in 2023, becoming one of the most successful expansion franchises in professional sports history with their rapid rise to contention.

Both teams will now prepare for the championship series, which will determine the 2026 Stanley Cup winner. The matchup brings together two organizations with different histories but similar recent success in building competitive rosters.

cards.headline: Hurricanes goalie Frederik Andersen plays day after agent's death
cards.teaser: Carolina goaltender Frederik Andersen took the ice in Game 5 against Montreal one day after his agent died by suicide.
cards.body:
Hurricanes goaltender Frederik Andersen played in Friday's Game 5 against the Canadiens just one day after his agent, Claude Lemieux, died by suicide. Despite the personal tragedy, Andersen delivered a strong performance as Carolina dominated with a 6-1 victory.

The win advanced the Hurricanes to the Stanley Cup Final, marking their first appearance in the championship series in two decades. Andersen's decision to play through grief underscored his commitment to his team during an emotionally challenging moment.

cards.headline: Indiana quarterback Brendan Sorsby bet on Hoosiers games while playing
cards.teaser: Former Indiana quarterback Brendan Sorsby placed at least 40 bets involving Indiana football during his time with the team.
cards.body:
Brendan Sorsby placed at least 40 bets on Indiana football while serving as the Hoosiers' quarterback, according to court documents filed Friday. He wagered approximately $90,000 over four years using sportsbook accounts registered to family members and friends.

The betting scheme involved multiple accounts to place wagers on games featuring his own team during his tenure with the Indiana football program.

cards.headline: Thunder forward Jalen Williams ruled out for Game 7 against Spurs
cards.teaser: Oklahoma City will be without forward Jalen Williams for Saturday's Game 7 against San Antonio due to injury.
cards.body:
Thunder wing Jalen Williams has been ruled out for Saturday's Game 7 against the Spurs. Williams, who has dealt with injuries throughout the season, will miss the decisive playoff matchup in Oklahoma City.

The Thunder will face the Spurs without a key contributor as they look to force a return to San Antonio. The winner of Game 7 will advance to the NBA Finals to face the New York Knicks.

cards.headline: Giants fear wide receiver Gunner Olszewski tore Achilles tendon
cards.teaser: New York Giants receiver Gunner Olszewski suffered a noncontact injury during practice that the team believes is a torn Achilles.
cards.body:
Giants wide receiver Gunner Olszewski suffered a noncontact injury during Friday's organized team activities. The team fears he has torn his Achilles tendon.

A torn Achilles typically requires an extended recovery period that could sideline a player for much of the season or longer. The Giants are awaiting test results to confirm the diagnosis.

cards.headline: UCLA's Megan Grant breaks school career home run record
cards.teaser: Megan Grant set a new UCLA career home run record as the Bruins routed Arkansas at the Women's College World Series.
cards.body:
Megan Grant made history at the Women's College World Series on Friday, breaking UCLA's career home run record. The milestone came during the Bruins' dominant performance against Arkansas, a matchup UCLA won 11-0 in a run-rule shortened game.

The offensive explosion was particularly notable in the second inning, when all nine batters in the UCLA lineup crossed home plate. Grant's record-breaking homer was part of this impressive display as the Bruins advanced through the tournament.

cards.headline: Giants teammates reconcile after dispute over Trump event
cards.teaser: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart and linebacker Abdul Carter expressed solidarity after a disagreement involving a Trump event.
cards.body:
Giants teammates Jaxson Dart and Abdul Carter expressed solidarity Friday following their disagreement over the quarterback's involvement in a Trump event. The two players publicly addressed the dispute, working to present a unified front after the incident created tension between them.

Both Carter and Dart spoke about the situation, emphasizing their professional relationship as they moved forward together.

hero.headline: Marcia Lucas, Oscar-Winning Star Wars Editor, Dies at 80
hero.body:
Marcia Lucas, the Oscar-winning film editor who helped shape Star Wars and other landmark films of the 1970s, died Wednesday in Rancho Mirage, California, following a battle with metastatic cancer. She was 80.

Lucasfilm posted a statement mourning her death. Lucas was one of three editors who shared an Academy Award for editing the original Star Wars film in 1977. Her work on the groundbreaking science fiction epic helped establish the visual language and pacing that defined the franchise.

Beyond Star Wars, Lucas edited several iconic films of the era. Her credits include American Graffiti and Taxi Driver, both of which showcased her skill in shaping narrative through cutting. She was married to Star Wars creator George Lucas at the time of the original trilogy's production, though the two later divorced.

Her editing contributions to Star Wars proved particularly influential. The film's fast-paced action sequences and emotional rhythms owed much to her decisions in the editing room. Along with her co-editors, she helped transform hours of footage into a coherent and thrilling adventure that would redefine popular cinema.

Lucas worked during a transformative period in American filmmaking. The 1970s saw a wave of director-driven films that challenged Hollywood conventions, and editors like Lucas played a crucial role in bringing those visions to the screen. Her work on Taxi Driver, directed by Martin Scorsese, demonstrated her versatility in handling both intimate character studies and large-scale spectacles.

The Oscar she received for Star Wars recognized not just technical proficiency but creative vision. The editing choices made during post-production helped establish the rhythm and energy that audiences responded to, turning a space fantasy into a cultural phenomenon.

Lucasfilm's tribute acknowledged her significant contributions to the Star Wars legacy. Her work on the original film laid the foundation for one of the most successful franchises in entertainment history, influencing generations of filmmakers and editors who followed.

cards.headline: Music Executive Clive Davis Hospitalized in New York
cards.teaser: The 94-year-old industry veteran was admitted to a New York City hospital with an upper respiratory infection.
cards.body:
Clive Davis, the legendary music executive, was hospitalized in New York City on Friday evening. The 94-year-old was admitted due to an upper respiratory infection.

Davis has shaped the careers of numerous artists over his decades-long career in the music industry. He is expected to recover soon from the respiratory issue that prompted his hospitalization.

cards.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Remaining 2026 Tour Dates
cards.teaser: The 92-year-old singer announced he is stepping away from the road to focus on health concerns.
cards.body:
Frankie Valli announced Friday that he is canceling all remaining concert dates for 2026 to focus on his health. The 92-year-old performer, who has maintained a passionate commitment to touring throughout his career, apologized to fans who purchased tickets for the scheduled shows.

Valli shared the decision on social media, expressing his regret about disappointing concertgoers. The move marks a significant shift for the veteran artist, who has been known for his dedication to performing on the road.

cards.headline: Multiple Artists Drop Out of Trump-Backed Freedom 250 Concert
cards.teaser: Over half the performers scheduled for the July 6 celebration on the National Mall have withdrawn.
cards.body:
At least seven of nine musical acts withdrew from the Freedom 250 concert series, a Trump administration event marking America's 250th anniversary. The departures occurred within 48 hours of the lineup announcement, with artists citing concerns about the event's atmosphere and threats being made.

Bret Michaels became the latest artist to exit the concert series. Bill Maher addressed the mounting cancellations during his Real Time show, dedicating a segment of his monologue to the troubled event.

cards.headline: Paul McCartney Reflects on Family During Beatles Fame
cards.teaser: The musician described how his family helped him navigate life during the height of Beatlemania.
cards.body:
Paul McCartney discussed how his family kept him grounded during the Beatles' rise to fame. The musician detailed a turning point during the band's period of unprecedented popularity and intense public attention.

McCartney explained how he navigated life under the spotlight while maintaining connections to his family. His reflections offered insight into how he managed the pressures that came with being part of one of the most popular musical groups in history.

cards.headline: Mountain Lion Tranquilized in Santa Monica Residential Area
cards.teaser: Wildlife officials removed the animal after it prompted a neighborhood lockdown and street closure.
cards.body:
A mountain lion was tranquilized and removed from a residential area in Santa Monica after closing 14th Street for most of the day. Wildlife officials tracked the animal through the neighborhood as residents remained on high alert.

The sighting prompted authorities to place the area on lockdown while they worked to safely capture and relocate the animal. Wildlife officials successfully tranquilized the mountain lion and removed it from the populated area.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Councilwoman Calls for Uncapped Film Tax Credits
cards.teaser: Nithya Raman urged gubernatorial candidates to support expanded incentives for film and TV production.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Councilwoman Nithya Raman called on candidates for governor to support uncapped tax incentives for film and television production. She appeared outside Radford Studios on Friday, days before the Tuesday election, with entertainment figures who support her mayoral campaign.

Raman was joined by Mike Schur, Cord Jefferson, and Kay Cannon at the event. She emphasized the need to ensure that Hollywood remains competitive as an industry center through expanded tax credit programs.

hero.headline: White House releases memo saying Trump in excellent health after physical
hero.body:
President Trump remains in excellent health following his annual medical examination, according to a memo released by the White House on Friday.

Trump visited Walter Reed National Military Medical Center on Tuesday for the routine checkup, where he underwent cardiac, neurological, dermatological and other medical evaluations. His physician characterized his overall health status as excellent and stated he is fully fit to carry out his duties as president.

The White House distributed the physician's memo to the press several days after the examination took place at the military facility. While the assessment provided an overall evaluation of the president's health, it did not include detailed findings from the specific examinations conducted during his visit.

Independent physicians not involved in Trump's care have questioned certain aspects of the health report. These medical experts have raised concerns about observable physical signs, specifically noting recurrent bruising on the president's hands and swelling in his legs. The independent doctors have suggested these symptoms warrant further investigation into what underlying conditions they might indicate.

Annual physical examinations are standard procedure for sitting U.S. presidents. During his visit to Walter Reed, Trump underwent comprehensive medical testing that assessed various bodily systems and functions. The multiple examinations conducted during his appointment reflected the thorough nature of presidential health screenings.

The physician's memo concluded that the president's health status supports his continued ability to fulfill the responsibilities of his office. The assessment was released to news organizations on Friday evening, making it public several days after the medical evaluation had been completed.

The timing of the memo's release and the gap between the actual examination and its public disclosure followed standard White House practices for sharing presidential health information with the media and the American public.

The release of Trump's health assessment continues a tradition of transparency regarding presidential medical status, though the specifics shared with the public typically remain limited to overall summaries rather than detailed clinical findings. The White House's characterization of the president's health as excellent stands in contrast to the concerns raised by independent medical professionals who have reviewed publicly available information about his physical condition.

The conflicting assessments highlight an ongoing tension between the official medical conclusions of the president's personal physicians and the observations of outside medical experts who have noted potential health concerns based on visible physical indicators.

cards.headline: US military kills three in strike on suspected drug boat in Pacific
cards.teaser: US Southern Command said the vessel was traveling along known narcotrafficking routes and operated by designated terrorist organizations.
cards.body:
The US military carried out a strike on Friday against a boat in the eastern Pacific Ocean, killing three men. US Southern Command said the vessel was involved in narco-trafficking operations and operated by a designated terrorist organization.

This marks the third such attack this week, bringing the overall death toll from the campaign above 200 people. The strikes are part of a months-long US military operation targeting alleged drug boats in the Caribbean Sea and eastern Pacific.

cards.headline: Federal judge allows Trump IRS lawsuit to reopen for review
cards.teaser: A Florida judge sided with intervenors who said a settlement creating an anti-weaponization fund tainted the case.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Florida agreed to reopen President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS. The decision sided with intervenors who challenged a settlement between Trump and the Department of Justice that would have dismissed the case in exchange for creating an "anti-weaponization" fund.

Meanwhile, a federal judge in Virginia temporarily blocked the Trump administration from transferring money into the $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund while legal challenges proceed. The order prevents the government from taking further action on the fund's creation or operation until arguments in the case are resolved.

cards.headline: Trump endorses Pam Evette over Rep. Nancy Mace in South Carolina governor race
cards.teaser: The president backed Lieutenant Governor Evette in a Truth Social post, calling her an America First Patriot who never wavered.
cards.body:
President Trump endorsed a GOP challenger to Rep. Nancy Mace's campaign for South Carolina governor, backing Lieutenant Governor Pam Evette in the contest.

The president called Evette an America First Patriot who never wavered in a Truth Social post. Trump wrote that Evette is a good friend, fighter, and winner. The endorsement represents a setback for Mace, who is running for the state's top executive position.

cards.headline: Southern Command chief meets with Cuban military officials
cards.teaser: The meeting near Naval Station Guantanamo Bay occurred as tensions between the two countries have heightened.
cards.body:
The head of US Southern Command met with senior leaders of the Cuban military amid heightened tensions between the two governments.

Commander Gen. Francis L. Donovan joined Cuba's First Deputy Minister of the Chief of the General Staff Roberto Legra Sotolongo and other leaders near Naval Station Guantanamo Bay. Southern Command announced the meeting, which took place as the Trump administration has increased pressure on the island.

cards.headline: Talarico leads Paxton by three points in Texas Senate poll
cards.teaser: A new poll shows the Democratic candidate with a slight edge over the Republican attorney general in the race.
cards.body:
State Rep. James Talarico has a slight lead over Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate race, according to a new poll released Friday.

Forty-seven percent of likely general election voters backed Talarico, compared with 44 percent for Paxton, in the poll from Texas Public Opinion Research. The survey was conducted following the runoff election.

cards.headline: Treasury Secretary Bessent endorses putting Trump on $250 bill
cards.teaser: Bessent voiced support for proposed currency to commemorate the US semiquincentennial during an interview at the Reagan Library.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the White House is pushing Congress to approve a $250 bill featuring President Trump's portrait to celebrate the nation's 250th anniversary of independence. The proposal would require changing federal law that currently prohibits living people from appearing on U.S. currency.

Bessent announced the initiative at a White House news conference, noting that the treasury has already begun preparing for the possible new currency. Democrats have vowed to block the measure in Congress.
